title: Speech Anatomy 3
text:
Voice Quality
Vocal Fry
Almost everything you’ve heard about “vocal fry” in popular culture is bunk.

There’s nothing harmful about it.
People really only complain about women doing it, even though men also do it (Slobe 2016)
When people complain, they often also don’t correctly identify what they’re complaining about.

title: Place & Manner

Place & Manner
Place

Where the point of greatest constriction is.

Manner

What happens at that place of constriction.

title: Place & Manner
text:
Place
Most articulations have an active and a passive articulator

Active: the articulator that moves
Passive: the articulator that gets moved to

Most places of articulation are named for the location of the passive articulator.

title: Place & Manner
text:
“Rhotics”
Rhotics aren’t a phonetically coherent set of sounds. Sounds classified as rhotics include

alveolar trills
uvular trills
uvular fricatives
velar fricatives
alveolar taps
retroflex approximants
alveolar approximants
whatever bunched [ɹ] is

title: Place & Manner
text:
“Rhotics”
As the name would suggest, these are sounds spelled with characters derived from Greek “\(\rho\)”.

title: Place & Manner
text:

Delattre, Pierre, and Donald C. Freeman. 1968. “A Dialect Study of American r’s by x-Ray Motion Picture.” Linguistics 6 (44). https://doi.org/10.1515/ling.1968.6.44.29.


Sproat, R, and O Fujimura. 1993. “Allophonic Variation in English /l/ and Its Implications for Phonetic Implementation.” Journal of Phonetics 21: 291–311.
